correctness.rationale: For n≥2, one-line ordinary successions S=Σ_{i<n}1{Π(i+1)=Π(i)+1} and C_j counts cycles of length j in that SAME permutation. Conditioning on arrows Π(i)=b and Π(i+1)=b+1 partitions into double-loops L, two-edge path P, and disjoint arrows D. Completion is uniform permutation on n-2 marked contracted objects. Expected j-cycles with s marks use C(2,s) C(m-2,j-s)/[j C(m,j)], so L_j=P_j=D_j=1/j in middle band 3≤j≤n-2. The boundary cases yield Cov(S,C_j)=[2 1(j=1)-1(j=2)-1(j=n-1)]/[n(n-1)]+1(j=n)/n², plus the stated sitewise spectrum for n≥5. Small n=2,3 checked separately and overlaps added. Exhaustive independent enumeration of 5912 permutations through size seven and 119 rational comparisons corroborated, while contraction counting proves all n. Zero covariance is not independence.

originality.rationale: The Reilly–Tanny counting of ordinary one-line successions is classical. Diaconis–Evans–Graham equate the marginal succession set law with a fixed-point subset in distribution, not joint law with cycles of the original Π. Mansour–Shattuck count successions inside disjoint-cycle notation; Foata-style correspondence changes cycle type, so cannot infer this same-permutation cycle-length covariance by relabeling. Earlier total cycle covariance 1/n² is credited and does not imply exact signed length-by-length cancellations. An unindexed marked-cycle cross-moment identity remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A classical joint permutation cycle-statistic identity may give the same marked-arrow covariance but be indexed under another terminology.
The prior scalar total-cycle covariance is not a novelty claim or evidence for a per-cycle-length formula.
No independence or weighted-Mallows extension follows from zero covariance.
